rules.cwe_name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
rules.description: Using a named argument whose name does not correspond to a parameter of the called function or method, will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
rules.description: Calling super with something other than the enclosing class may cause incorrect object initialization.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: Using too many or too few arguments in a call to the `__init__` method of a class will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Finds uses of symmetric cryptography algorithms that are weak, obsolete, or otherwise unaccepted. The key lengths allowed are 128, 192, and 256 bits. These are all the key lengths supported by AES, so any application of AES is considered acceptable.

rules.cwe_name: Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
rules.description: Handling 'BaseException' means that system exits and keyboard interrupts may be mis-handled.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
rules.description: Building a SQL query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious SQL code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Security checks on the substrings of an unparsed URL are often vulnerable to bypassing.

rules.cwe_name: Security Issue (CWE-730)
rules.description: User input should not be used in regular expressions without first being escaped, otherwise a malicious user may be able to inject an expression that could require exponential time on certain inputs.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
rules.description: Building a NoSQL query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious NoSQL code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Data Processing Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.
